text.p: World champion Jansher Khan survived a daunting experience in front of a hostile Egyptian crowd to reach the semifinals of the Gezira Open squash championship on Wednesday.
Jansher beat local hero Ahmed Barada, the 19-year-old former world junior champion, 15-5 8-15 15-4 15-14 in 81 minutes but was unimpressed by the behaviour of his opponent or the home supporters.

"When you play Barada in Egypt he is constantly putting pressure on the referee and exciting his supporters to do the same. The audiences here idolise him and applaud every appeal however right or wrong it may be," said the Pakistani.
"He makes a fight of it and some day someone is going to be mad enough to hit him."
One female fan threw water at the marker, Nasser Zarhran, when Barada was denied a let at 14-14 in the fourth game, but the young Egyptian claimed it was his opponent who had lost his cool.
"He was the one pressurising the referee. Perhaps he is feeling the pressure. He is not the player he was three years ago."
Australian second seed Rodney Eyles, who also reached the semifinals, was among those who feared the situation might escalate out of control.

"It would be in my interest to see Jansher lose in a quarter-final and lose a few ranking points," he said. "But I was willing him to avoid losing under the circumstances that were in play here tonight."
Pakistan's Zubair Jahan Khan received a walkover into the last four when the seventh seed Mark Chaloner of England withdrew with severe food poisoning.
